items.headline: Fed holds at 4.00% in a hawkish 10-2 vote; GDP beats, core PCE runs hot, and a fourth voice joins the hike chorus
items.summary: The FOMC held the funds rate at 3.75-4.00% with both dissenters (Cook, Hammack) wanting a hike, not a cut; new Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference gave no December guidance. Q3 GDP beat at +3.4% (cons. ~3.2%) and core PCE ran hot at +0.3% m/m/3.1% y/y, while Richmond Fed's Barkin became a fourth hawkish voice over the weekend alongside Friday's Musalem/Logan/Daly.
items.actionable: A confirmed hawkish hold (not just hawkish rhetoric) plus strong growth data removes the dovish-pivot excuse, reinforcing the case for staying cash-heavy and cautious on duration into December.

items.headline: BOJ and ECB both deliver hawkish holds -- Ueda flags a likely December hike, Lagarde announces early resignation
items.summary: BOJ held at 1.25% (8-1, Takata dissenting for an immediate hike) with Governor Ueda explicitly signaling strong December-hike prospects as inflation hit the 2% target for the first time since 2013. The ECB held 2.65%/2.50% unanimously in a hawkish hold, with Lagarde surprising markets by announcing she will resign as ECB President in February 2027, ahead of her term's expiry.
items.actionable: This turns the hawkish story into a synchronized three-central-bank signal rather than a Fed-only one -- a genuine incremental headwind for global duration and carry trades, worth monitoring for JPY-sensitive and European exposure.

items.headline: S&P cuts Meta's credit outlook to negative; OpenAI trims new funding round by $10B
items.summary: S&P Global revised Meta's credit outlook to negative on AI-capex cash-flow risk, projecting roughly $39B (2026) and $71B (2027) free-cash-flow deficits. Separately, OpenAI reportedly cut its new funding-round target by $10B to about $20B at a $1.25T valuation after some backers trimmed commitments.
items.actionable: The AI-capex-credibility shock that hit Amazon/Intel on Friday is now visible in credit ratings and private AI fundraising too -- a reason to stay cautious on richly-valued AI-capex-exposed tech rather than treat Friday as a one-day air pocket.

items.headline: Bitcoin stabilizes near $77,000-77,500 as Binance recovers ~90% of hacked funds; FBI blames North Korea
items.summary: Binance said it has replenished about 90% of the $6.3B stolen in Friday's record hack and resumed withdrawals on Nov 1. The FBI formally attributed the attack to North Korea's Lazarus Group (TraderTraitor). Bitcoin has ticked up to roughly $77,000-77,500, off Friday's ~$76,500-76,815 low, while the crypto Fear & Greed Index remains flat at 30 (Fear) for a second straight day.
items.actionable: Early stabilization, not healing -- state-actor attribution keeps regulatory/exchange-scrutiny tail risk alive, so this is a reason to stay minimally exposed to crypto rather than chase the bounce.

items.headline: Gold craters to ~$3,885 and silver breaks below $50 on liquidation selling; HSBC cuts 2027 silver forecast
items.summary: Gold fell 3.63% and silver 5.86% to an 11-month low (~$49.14) as rate-driven real-yield repricing and margin-call liquidation from the tech rout hit precious metals together. Over the weekend, HSBC cut its 2027 average silver forecast to $64/oz from $71/oz, citing weakening industrial and jewelry demand.
items.actionable: A fresh bearish sell-side data point layered on Friday's selloff -- for a levered-silver-heavy book, size risk conservatively into Monday rather than treat Friday's drop as a pure technical overshoot.

items.headline: Iran rejects Qatar's Hormuz mediation draft as CENTCOM disputes Iran's tanker-mine claim
items.summary: Iran rejected Qatar's new draft deal as 'unacceptable,' with Tehran saying it will not concede on its nuclear program, though it remains open to its own 7-day plan to reopen the strait. Separately, US CENTCOM publicly disputed Iran's claim that tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, calling it disinformation and stating major transit lanes remain clear.
items.actionable: No de-escalation heading into the new week -- keeps both the oil risk premium and the safe-haven gold/silver bid alive; don't expect a quick relief rally, but also no change needed to the existing precious-metals thesis.

items.headline: Putin agrees in principle to resume US-Ukraine-Russia trilateral talks
items.summary: Russian President Putin reportedly agreed in principle to resume trilateral peace talks after Nov 10, with technical-level talks tentatively pencilled for Abu Dhabi during Nov 6-10 (date/venue unconfirmed).
items.actionable: A slow-moving, second geopolitical track that could reduce the broader macro risk premium if it progresses -- not actionable this week, but worth tracking alongside the Nov 10 rare-earth deadline.

items.headline: Oil set for fourth straight monthly gain as Hormuz risk premium holds near 13-month highs; OPEC+ meets on quotas
items.summary: Oil is on track for a fourth consecutive monthly gain with the Hormuz-driven risk premium near 13-month highs. OPEC+'s seven core members held their scheduled Nov 1 meeting to set December quotas, with Gulf producers reportedly pumping below target amid continuing Hormuz-related export disruption; the meeting's formal outcome was not yet confirmed as of writing.
items.actionable: Watch the OPEC+ readout at Asia's open Monday -- a hold/cut into continued Hormuz disruption would reinforce the energy risk premium already priced into the book's commodity exposure.

items.headline: China's Nov 10 rare-earth truce deadline still has no matching legal text from Beijing
items.summary: With the rare-earth-specific export-control suspension due to expire Nov 10 (9 days out), China has still not published the legal text formalizing the suspension, even though MOFCOM confirmed the broader US-China trade truce runs to Jan 10, 2027.
items.actionable: The binary catalyst stays live into the new week -- no change warranted to rare-earth watchlist positioning, but this is the single most important date on the book's near-term catalyst calendar.

items.headline: MP Materials and rare-earth peers slide alongside the broader margin-call liquidation
items.summary: MP Materials fell about 6% and rare-earth peers slid as the same margin-call liquidation that hit precious metals and tech spilled into the sector.
items.actionable: A liquidation-driven move rather than a thesis change -- the ex-China rare-earth re-rating case into Nov 10 is intact, but near-term volatility should be expected.

items.headline: Tencent and Alibaba in advanced talks to invest in DeepSeek as valuation jumps sevenfold
items.summary: Tencent and Alibaba are reportedly in talks to invest in DeepSeek at a valuation above $20B -- up roughly sevenfold from about $3B a year ago. Both already run in-house models and have backed other Chinese AI labs (Zhipu, MiniMax, Moonshot).
items.actionable: A stock-specific positive for HK tech optionality on China AI monetization, but it doesn't offset the broader AI-capex-credibility concerns dragging global tech since Friday -- treat as color, not a reason to add broad HK tech beta.

items.headline: SMIC posts 29% profit jump and revenue beat on AI and Huawei chip demand
items.summary: SMIC reported a 29% profit jump and a revenue beat, driven by AI and Huawei chip demand.
items.actionable: A fundamental positive for the HK-tech sleeve's chip exposure, independent of Friday's global AI-capex sentiment shock.

items.headline: Singapore banks stay pressured into Nov 5-6 Q3 results as yields hold at 4.4-4.5%
items.summary: Singapore's banks remain under pressure heading into Q3 results due Nov 5-6, with local yields holding at 4.4-4.5%.
items.actionable: Key near-term catalyst for the SGX bank sleeve -- watch Nov 5-6 results for net-interest-margin commentary given yields holding at multi-month highs.
